Include cube-size selectors for 2x2, 3x3, 4x4, and 5x5; move count and timer; Scramble, Undo, Hint, and Reset controls; and a compact formula/tip panel. history.critique: Brief & Intent: All required modules exist (2x2–5x5 selectors, timer/moves, Scramble/Undo/Hint/Reset, tips panel), but the centerpiece fails its core job. The selector shows 3x3 active yet the cube renders 2x2-scale stickers (4 per face); the top face is a mix of white/blue/yellow while the Moves panel says 'Not scrambled'; and the Sticker Map legend (Front=green, Left=blue, Back=purple) contradicts the visible faces (front=yellow, left=white, bottom=purple). Three sources of truth — selector, state text, legend — all disagree with the render, which is fatal for a puzzle product. Clarity: the focal cube, which the brief says must carry 'spatial clarity,' reads as floating rounded cards: stickers protrude past the cube silhouette (top and left), a red sliver z-fights between the yellow and blue faces, and gaps between stickers are large and uneven, so face planes are ambiguous. The size labels are truncated to unreadable fragments ('POC..', 'CLA..', 'MAS..', 'PRO..'), and the orange dot indicators on each panel have no explained meaning. Craft: sticker border-radius is far too large for cube stickers, producing pill shapes instead of a coherent colored face; faces are not coplanar under the perspective, warping into separate panels; there is no ground shadow or per-face shading to anchor dimensionality; the 'solved' initial state is not actually solved. Expressiveness: the identity elements are genuinely good — isometric logo, keycap badges, orange gradient primary action, and authored tips (superscript notation, 4x4/5x5 parity) — but the hero moment is janky, so the product's signature is undermined exactly where it should be strongest. Real trade-offs: soft rounding vs. grid fidelity (rounding must lose), dramatic perspective vs. face legibility (a longer perspective distance / fixed isometric tilt wins), and a custom color scheme vs. legend coherence (the legend must be generated from the actual orientation).
history.suggestion: Prioritized plan, in order: 1) Rebuild the cube as a true N×N grid synced to the active selector — 9 stickers per face at 3x3, 4 at 2x2, etc. — with uniform 2–4px gaps, small radius (~6–8px on ~120px stickers), and stickers inset within each face so nothing protrudes; make faces exactly coplanar to kill the red sliver. 2) Make state consistent: start fully solved with each face a single color, timer/moves at zero, and have only Scramble mix faces; replace the placeholder Moves text with a live notation readout (e.g., 'R U' F2') plus a short history strip so the brief's 'formula' requirement is visibly met. 3) Reconcile the Sticker Map: assign legend colors to the actual face positions (or regenerate labels from the current orientation) so Front/Right/Up always match what is on screen. 4) Strengthen the 3D presentation: increase perspective distance or lock a fixed isometric tilt (~-24° X / 45° Y), add per-face brightness (top 100%, front ~90%, side ~80%) and a soft elliptical ground shadow to sell dimensionality, and add a subtle idle float/rotation as the memorable moment. 5) Fix the size selector: full labels (Pocket / Classic / Master / Pro) or bare dimensions, larger hit areas, and a clear selected ring, keeping the grid icons. 6) Tactile polish: hover/active/focus-visible states on all buttons and size chips, consistent keycap badges. 7) Preserve the existing dark palette, monospace type system, and orange-as-primary-only rule; keep the tips panel content as-is since it is the most authored element. This keeps every required feature, restores the cube as the unambiguous focal point, and turns the janky hero into the product's signature.
